newsitem.title: GERMANY: INTERVIEW - Hoechst - dlr level lifted profit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Hoechst - dlr level lifted profit.

text.p: More than half of German chemical group Hoechst's 1997 operating profit growth in the first half came from the current strength of the dollar, Klaus-Juergen Schmieder, chief financial officer, said on Wednesday.
"Over half of the seven percent growth in operating profit on a comparable basis came from the strength of the dollar," Schmieder told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Schmieder said Hoechst had raised its forecast for the dollar/mark level for this year to 1.70 marks from 1.65 marks and that if the dollar stayed at its current high level then Hoechst would see stronger earnings growth in 1997.
"Naturally, however, other competitive conditions could change and dampen this effect," Schmieder said, admitting that Hoechst policy in this area was "cautious".
The dollar stood at around 1.85 marks on Wednesday.

Operating profit fell 18 percent to 2.27 billion marks from 2.775 billion marks in the first half of 1997, but rose on a comparable basis by seven percent. Earnings fell because of one-off income in 1996.
Schmieder said that because of extraordinary income from disposals last year, the group hoped to at least match the earnings growth of the first half of the year.
"If we can maintain the operating earnings growth of seven percent seen in the first half of the year, then we would be very happy," Schmieder said.
Schmieder said volumes on a compaable basis would grow by around two percent, while growth in prices was mixed as certain areas, such as polyester, were under pressure, while others were improving.
